id_forge.info.uuidv4: UUID v4 — Fully random identifier. Best for distributed systems where uniqueness matters more than order. Widest compatibility.
id_forge.info.uuidv7: UUID v7 — Time-ordered identifier (timestamp + random bits). Ideal for database indexing (B-trees). Faster inserts than v4.
id_forge.info.ulid: ULID — 26-char Crockford Base32 identifier. Time-sortable, URL-safe, human-readable. Compact and easy to copy.
id_forge.info.nanoid: NanoID — Short, URL-safe 21-character ID. 64-symbol alphabet. Great for sessions, short links, filenames.
id_forge.info.swhid: SWHID — ISO/IEC 18670 content identifier. Computed from SHA1 & SHA-256 hash for integrity. Used by Software Heritage for code archiving.

page.about:
About RedoSan Authenticity

What is RedoSan Authenticity?

RedoSan Authenticity is a free, open-source, client-side digital authenticity toolkit. It provides a comprehensive suite of tools for watermarking, fingerprinting, forensic analysis, provenance tracking, and content verification — all running entirely in your browser or via a Node.js CLI. No files are ever uploaded to any server; every operation happens locally on your machine.

Why Was It Built?

Digital content authenticity is increasingly critical in an age of AI-generated media, deepfakes, and misinformation. Existing solutions often require uploading sensitive files to third-party servers or expensive commercial software. RedoSan Authenticity was created to provide a free, private, and comprehensive alternative that puts control back in the hands of creators, journalists, and forensic analysts.

Complete Tool Suite

  • Image Watermarking — 9 algorithms (LSB, DCT, Zero-bit, Fragile, Neural SS, Multi-bit, Patchwork, Adaptive, Statistical) for embedding and extracting invisible watermarks
  • Audio Watermarking — 8 algorithms (LSB, Phase Coding, Echo Hiding, DSSS, QIM, DWT Haar, Patchwork, DCT) for embedding data in WAV audio files
  • Document Watermarking — Embed watermarks into TXT, DOCX, and PDF files using Zero-Width Characters, homoglyph substitution, whitespace encoding, line-shift, and word-shift techniques
  • Pixel Injection — 23 algorithms across 4 categories (spatial, frequency, deep learning, and professional) for advanced pixel-level data embedding
  • Fingerprinting — 17 cryptographic hash algorithms (SHA-1/2/3, BLAKE2/3, MD5, RIPEMD-160, Whirlpool) plus 4 perceptual hashes (aHash, dHash, pHash, wHash)
  • C2PA Provenance — Read, write, and verify C2PA Content Credentials with ECDSA signing for JPEG and PNG files
  • Decentralized Identity (DID) — Generate Ed25519, ECDSA P-256, and RSA key pairs with full W3C DID Document creation
  • OpenTimestamps — Create, verify, and upgrade blockchain-anchored timestamps using the OpenTimestamps protocol
  • Digital Certificates — Generate authenticity passports in PDF, DOCX, and EPUB formats with QR code verification
  • Forensic Analysis — Error Level Analysis (ELA), noise heatmaps, JPEG marker inspection, and metadata anomaly detection
  • Metadata Reader — Extract EXIF, XMP, IPTC, and PNG chunk metadata from images
  • File Converter — Convert between image, audio, video, document, and subtitle formats using ffmpeg.wasm
  • ID Forge — Generate UUID v4/v7, ULID, NanoID, and SWHID identifiers in bulk
  • Assistant — Built-in chatbot for guided help and troubleshooting

Technical Architecture

The application is built entirely with vanilla JavaScript — no frameworks, no build tools, no backend. It runs as a Progressive Web App (PWA) with offline support via Service Worker caching. The same algorithms power both the browser interface and the Node.js CLI, ensuring consistent results across environments.

All cryptographic operations use the Web Cryptography API (crypto.subtle) in the browser and Node.js native crypto in the CLI. Image manipulation uses the HTML5 Canvas API. Document processing uses JSZip for DOCX, PDF-lib for PDF manipulation, and jsPDF for PDF generation. Audio processing uses raw PCM data manipulation with FFT transforms implemented from scratch.

Who Is It For?

  • Journalists and fact-checkers — Verify the authenticity of images and documents before publication
  • Photographers and artists — Protect your work with invisible watermarks and prove ownership
  • Forensic analysts — Detect tampering, analyze compression artifacts, and examine metadata anomalies
  • Developers — Integrate authenticity checks into your workflow via the CLI or browser APIs
  • Legal professionals — Generate verifiable digital passports and timestamps for evidence preservation
  • Content creators — Establish provenance chains for your digital content from creation to publication

Privacy by Design

Privacy is not a feature — it is the foundation. RedoSan Authenticity processes everything locally in your browser. No images, no metadata, no personal information ever leaves your device. The only network requests are for loading CDN-hosted libraries (with SRI integrity checks) and contacting OpenTimestamps calendar servers (for timestamp creation and verification).

Open Source

RedoSan Authenticity is fully open source under the GNU General Public License v2.0. The complete source code is available on GitHub. Contributions, bug reports, and feature requests are welcome.

Internationalization

The interface is available in 8 languages: العربية (Arabic), Deutsch (German), English, Español (Spanish), Français (French), 日本語 (Japanese), 한국어 (Korean), and 中文 (Chinese). Right-to-left (RTL) layout is fully supported for Arabic.

Version

Current version: v1.6 — featuring Multi-Page Architecture (MPA), standalone tool pages, Document Watermarking, Audio Watermarking, DID, C2PA, Digital Certificates, File Converter, and 277+ unit tests across 35 test files with 40+ CI/CD workflows.
page.privacy:
Privacy Policy

Last updated: June 2026

Our Commitment to Privacy

RedoSan Authenticity is designed to be 100% private by default. The application runs entirely client-side — in your browser or via the Node.js CLI. No files, metadata, personal information, or analytics data are ever collected, stored, or transmitted to any server. Every watermark, fingerprint, timestamp, and certificate is generated locally on your machine.

Data Collection

We collect nothing. RedoSan Authenticity has no backend server, no database, no user accounts, no tracking cookies, no analytics service, and no telemetry. The application is hosted statically on GitHub Pages and all processing occurs in your browser's JavaScript runtime or the Node.js CLI environment.

  • No uploads: Files you process are never sent over the network
  • No cookies: The application does not set or read any tracking or analytics cookies
  • No localStorage: User preferences (theme, language) are stored in your browser's localStorage for convenience only and never transmitted
  • No accounts: There is no registration, authentication, or user profiling

How It Works

When you upload a file to any tool in RedoSan Authenticity, the file is read into your browser's memory using the HTML5 File API. All subsequent processing — hashing, watermark embedding, pixel manipulation, metadata extraction, timestamp creation, certificate generation — happens entirely within the JavaScript runtime of your browser. The processed result is offered as a downloadable file or displayed on screen. No data is written to any disk on the server, nor is any data transmitted over the network (with the explicit exception of OpenTimestamps, described below).

Network Requests

The application makes the following network requests, all of which are necessary for functionality:

  • CDN library loading: JavaScript libraries (jsPDF, JSZip, PDF-lib, QRious, LameJS, FFmpeg.wasm) are loaded from cdnjs and jsdelivr CDNs. All loaded scripts use Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes to ensure they have not been tampered with. These CDNs may log standard HTTP request metadata (IP address, User-Agent, requested file) in accordance with their own privacy policies. No data from your files is included in these requests.
  • OpenTimestamps: When creating a timestamp, the SHA-256 hash of your file (not the file itself) is sent to OpenTimestamps calendar servers to be anchored in the Bitcoin blockchain. The original file content cannot be reconstructed from this hash. Verification and upgrade requests similarly send only hash data.
  • Service Worker: The application registers a Service Worker for offline caching and security enforcement. The SW operates entirely within your browser and does not communicate with any external server beyond the initial page load.
  • GitHub Pages hosting: The application is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub may collect standard server logs in accordance with their Privacy Statement.

Third-Party Code

The following third-party libraries are loaded and executed client-side:

  • jsPDF — PDF generation for certificates and reports
  • JSZip — DOCX file creation and extraction
  • PDF-lib — PDF manipulation for document watermarking
  • QRious — QR code generation for certificates
  • LameJS — MP3 encoding for audio processing
  • FFmpeg.wasm — File format conversion
  • OpenTimestamps.js — Timestamp creation and verification

All libraries are loaded with SRI integrity hashes. No library has access to your files beyond what is explicitly passed to it by the application code. All libraries execute in your browser's sandboxed JavaScript environment.

Security

  • Content Security Policy: The application enforces a strict CSP that restricts script sources, prevents inline script execution, and blocks connections to untrusted origins.
  • Subresource Integrity: All CDN-loaded scripts and stylesheets are verified against SHA-384 integrity hashes before execution.
  • Service Worker: The SW acts as a security layer, blocking 68+ dangerous file extensions, enforcing a JavaScript file whitelist, and detecting embedded URLs at multiple encoding levels.
  • Domain origin check: All JavaScript files verify they are executing on the expected domain (redo-san.github.io, localhost, or 127.0.0.1) and silently refuse to run on untrusted domains.
  • File validation: Uploaded files are validated against a 6-layer security pipeline including extension blocklist, magic byte verification, content scanning, and document threat detection.

Children's Privacy

RedoSan Authenticity does not knowingly collect any personal information from children. The application is not directed at children under the age of 13. As no data is collected from any user at any age, there is no risk of inadvertent data collection from minors.

Changes to This Policy

This privacy policy may be updated occasionally to reflect changes in the application or legal requirements. The date of the last update will always be displayed at the top of this page. Continued use of the tool after any changes constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

Contact

If you have questions about this privacy policy or the privacy practices of RedoSan Authenticity, please open an issue on GitHub or start a discussion in the Discussions section.

wm.embed_help:
Embed a hidden digital watermark into an image to protect your content.

Upload a cover image using the file selector below. Then choose or type a secret message — this is the data that will be hidden inside the image. Pick a watermark algorithm from the dropdown menu; each algorithm offers different trade-offs between capacity, robustness against attacks, and visual invisibility. A password is optional but adds an extra layer of security.

Click the Embed button to start the process. Once complete, the watermarked image is displayed alongside a quality report showing PSNR and SSIM scores so you can evaluate how much the image changed.

⚠️ Important: Download your results before navigating away. Use the Download button below the results to save the watermarked image or a report in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format. Results are stored only in your current browser session and will be lost if you leave this page.
wm.extract_help:
Extract a hidden message from a watermarked image to reveal its secret content.

Upload the watermarked image (stego image) using the file selector. Select the algorithm that was used during embedding — if you are unsure, choose Auto Detect and the system will scan all available algorithms to find a match. If a password was used during embedding, enter the same password here.

Click the Extract button to retrieve the hidden message. The extracted data will be displayed in the results area below.

⚠️ Important: Download your results before navigating away. Use the Download button to save the extracted data in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format. Results are stored only in your current browser session.
awm.embed_help_title: How to embed an audio watermark
awm.embed_help:
Hide a secret message inside an audio file using digital audio watermarking.

Upload a WAV audio file as the carrier. Type or upload a secret message to hide within the audio. Choose a watermark algorithm from the dropdown — each algorithm balances audio quality, data capacity, and resistance to compression or signal processing. A password adds protection against unauthorised extraction.

Click Embed to process. The watermarked audio file will be available for download along with a quality report.

⚠️ Important: Download your results before navigating away. Use the Download button to save the watermarked audio or a report in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format. Results are session-only and will be lost on exit.
awm.extract_help_title: How to extract an audio watermark
awm.extract_help:
Reveal a hidden message from a watermarked audio file.

Upload the watermarked audio file using the file selector. Choose the same algorithm that was used during embedding. If a password was set, enter it now.

Click Extract to retrieve the hidden message. The extracted data appears in the results area.

⚠️ Important: Download your results before leaving the page. Use the Download button to save in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
pi.embed_help_title: How to inject a pixel watermark
pi.embed_help:
Embed a secret payload into image pixels using advanced injection algorithms.

Upload a carrier image. Enter your secret payload — this can be text, a file, or a message. Select an injection category and algorithm from the menus; each category (spatial, frequency, deep learning, professional) offers different levels of capacity, invisibility, and robustness. Adjust advanced options such as embedding strength, password, and redundancy as needed.

Click Inject to embed the payload. The result includes metrics like PSNR, SSIM, and BER to evaluate quality and robustness.

⚠️ Important: Download your results before navigating away. Use the Download button to save the injected image or a report in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
pi.extract_help_title: How to extract a pixel payload
pi.extract_help:

Upload the image containing the hidden payload. Select the same algorithm category and algorithm used during injection. If a password was set, provide it.

Click Extract to retrieve the hidden data. The extracted payload appears in the results area.

⚠️ Important: Download your extracted data before leaving. Use the Download button to save in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
pi.analyze_help_title: How to analyse an image for watermarks
pi.analyze_help:
Analyse an image to detect the presence of hidden watermarks or injected data.

Upload an image for analysis. The system runs statistical tests, blind decoding, and optional machine-learning detection to identify watermark traces. Results show detection confidence, estimated algorithm, and robustness scores.

Use this tool when you suspect an image contains hidden data but do not know which algorithm was used.

⚠️ Important: Download the analysis report before navigating away. Use the Download button to save in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
fp.help:
Generate cryptographic hashes and perceptual fingerprints for any file.

Upload a file using the file selector. The system automatically computes all supported hash algorithms including SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-3, BLAKE2, BLAKE3, MD5, RIPEMD-160, Whirlpool, and perceptual image hashes (aHash, dHash, pHash, wHash).

Each hash uniquely identifies the file content. Compare hashes across systems to verify file integrity. Perceptual hashes can detect visually similar images even after resizing or compression.

⚠️ Important: Download the fingerprint report before navigating away. Use the Download button to save the results in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
md.help:
Extract and display metadata embedded in image files.

Upload an image file (JPEG recommended for EXIF data). The system reads standard metadata tags including camera make and model, GPS coordinates, date and time, image dimensions, colour profile, and any embedded thumbnails.

This tool is useful for verifying image origin, checking for editing history, and extracting location data from photographs.

⚠️ Important: Download the metadata report before navigating away. Use the Download button to save in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
ts.create_help:
Create a cryptographic timestamp for any file using the OpenTimestamps protocol.

Upload a file to timestamp. The system computes the file hash and submits it to the Bitcoin blockchain via the OpenTimestamps network. This creates a permanent, verifiable proof that the file existed at a specific point in time.

Once the timestamp is created, download the .ots file. Keep this file alongside the original — you will need both for future verification.

⚠️ Important: Download the .ots file before navigating away. You can also save a report in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
ts.verify_help:
Verify that a file matches its OpenTimestamp proof.

Upload the original file and its corresponding .ots proof file. The system re-computes the file hash and compares it against the timestamp proof.

If the verification succeeds, it confirms the file existed unchanged since the timestamp date. If it fails, the file may have been modified after the timestamp was created.

⚠️ Important: Download the verification report before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
did.create_help:
Create a Decentralized Identifier (DID) and its associated DID document.

Select a cryptographic key type (Ed25519, ECDSA P-256, or RSA). The system generates the key pair and constructs a DID document containing the public key, verification methods, and service endpoints.

The DID document can be exported for use with distributed ledgers or other verifiable data registries. Store the private key securely — it cannot be recovered if lost.

⚠️ Important: Download the DID document before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, or HTML format.
did.sign_help_title: How to sign with a DID
did.sign_help:
Sign a message or file using your DID private key to prove authorship.

Enter or upload your DID private key. Then provide the message or file you want to sign. The system generates a digital signature that cryptographically proves you authored the content.

Share the signature alongside the content so others can verify it using your DID document's public key.

⚠️ Important: Download the signature file before navigating away. Save it in JSON or TXT format.
did.verify_help_title: How to verify a DID signature
did.verify_help:
Verify a digital signature created with a DID.

Upload the original message or file, the signature file, and the DID document containing the public key. The system checks whether the signature matches the content and the public key.

A successful verification confirms the content was signed by the DID owner and has not been tampered with.

⚠️ Important: Download the verification report before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, or HTML format.
c2pa.read_help:
Read C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) data from an image.

Upload an image file that contains C2PA provenance metadata. The system parses the C2PA manifest and displays the digital signature, content credentials, editing history, and any claims made by the content creator.

Use this tool to verify the origin and editing history of images from C2PA-compatible cameras and editing software.

⚠️ Important: Download the C2PA report before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, or HTML format.
c2pa.write_help:
Add C2PA provenance data to an image, creating a verifiable content credential.

Upload an image and provide creator information such as name, organisation, and assertions about the content. Select a content type (artwork, news, photography, etc.) to categorise the credential. The system creates a C2PA manifest and signs it using an ECDSA key embedded in your browser.

The signed image can be shared with others, who can verify its provenance using the C2PA read tool.

⚠️ Important: Download the C2PA-signed image before navigating away. You can also save the manifest in JSON format.
c2pa.verify_help_title: How to verify a C2PA signature
c2pa.verify_help:
Verify the cryptographic signature of a C2PA-provenanced image.

Upload a C2PA-signed image. The system extracts the manifest and validates the ECDSA signature against the embedded public key. It also checks the integrity of the metadata and reports any tampering.

A successful verification confirms the image has not been altered since its C2PA credentials were created.

⚠️ Important: Download the verification report before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, or HTML format.
cert.help_title: How to create a digital passport
cert.help:
Generate a comprehensive digital passport certificate for your digital assets.

Fill in the asset details: asset name, owner, description, and any applicable licence or rights information. Upload the asset file and optionally add a watermark result, fingerprint result, timestamp proof, or C2PA provenance as supporting evidence.

The system generates a formatted certificate document that can serve as a proof of authenticity for your digital creations.

⚠️ Important: Download the certificate before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, EPUB, or HTML format.
forensic.help_title: How to use the forensic analyser
forensic.help:
Analyse an image for signs of tampering, manipulation, or forensic artefacts.

Upload an image for forensic analysis. The system runs multiple detection techniques including Error Level Analysis (ELA), noise analysis, JPEG marker inspection, and metadata anomaly detection.

Results highlight regions of potential manipulation and provide a tampering confidence score. Use this tool to verify image authenticity in journalistic, legal, or investigative contexts.

⚠️ Important: Download the forensic report before navigating away. Save it in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
conv.help:
Convert files between different formats using the built-in converter.

Upload a file and select the target format. Supported conversions include image formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF), audio formats (WAV, MP3, OGG), video formats (MP4, WebM, AVI), document formats (TXT, HTML, Markdown), and subtitle formats (SRT, VTT).

Image and document conversions happen entirely in your browser. Audio and video conversions use ffmpeg.wasm and run locally on your device.

⚠️ Important: Download your converted file before navigating away. Converted files exist only in your browser memory.
rt.help:
Detect and remove digital watermarks from images, audio files, and documents.

Select the type of watermark you want to detect (digital watermark, audio watermark, pixel injection, or document watermark). Upload the file and select the specific removal technique appropriate for your case.

The system analyses the file and attempts to remove or neutralise the detected watermark. Note that removal success depends on the strength and algorithm of the original watermark.

⚠️ Important: Download the processed file before navigating away. Save it in the available format.
id_forge.help:
Generate various types of unique identifiers for software development and data management.

Select an identifier type from the dropdown: UUID v4 (random), UUID v7 (time-ordered), ULID, Nano ID (configurable length), or SWHID (Software Heritage Identifier). Configure any type-specific options such as ID count or Nano ID length.

For SWHID, choose the input method — upload a file, type text, or fetch a URL. The system computes the appropriate hash and constructs the identifier.

⚠️ Important: Download your generated identifiers before navigating away. Save them in PDF, DOCX, JSON, CSV, TXT, XML, or HTML format.
docw.embed_help:
Hide a secret message inside a text document using document watermarking techniques.

Upload a document (TXT, DOCX, or PDF) as the carrier. Enter your secret message. Choose a watermarking technique from the dropdown: whitespace encoding, zero-width characters, homoglyph substitution, line-shift, or word-shift. A password adds extra protection.

Click Embed to process. The watermarked document preserves the original visible text while carrying the hidden message.

⚠️ Important: Download the watermarked document before navigating away. Save it in DOCX or PDF format. You can also export a report in TXT, CSV, XML, or HTML format.
docw.extract_help_title: How to extract a document watermark
docw.extract_help:
Read a hidden message from a watermarked document.

Upload the watermarked document (TXT, DOCX, or PDF). Select the technique that was used during embedding. If a password was set, enter it.

Click Extract to retrieve the hidden message. The extracted text appears in the results area.

⚠️ Important: Download the extracted data before leaving. Save it in TXT, CSV, XML, HTML, or as a DOCX or PDF report.
